proofs: EC5C1 masks EDX to 15 bits; EC5CC copies it to EAX. EC5D4 ANDs with 0x80000007, so SF=0. Only MOVs intervene before JNS; its three-instruction negative correction cannot execute.

Spiral EBP starts at 1 and increases by 2 only after a round. The counter starts at 0 and permits reentry only below 228, so every reached direction has positive span 1..455. Its four JLE skip edges cannot execute.

Chooser remainder is (first & 32767) % 100, hence 0..99. Every native weight row sums to 100; some cumulative comparison must succeed by row 3. The ECX==4 loop exit is unreachable without private-stack/code corruption.

caller_bridge.retained: Full EAX, RET0 ESP movement and nonvolatile registers.
caller_bridge.scratch: ECX and flags are overwritten immediately at the animal callsites. EDX is replaced along the join branches; the 49F108 path calls the typed two-DWORD movement helper before its next EDX use. 41CD5A reloads EDX and ECX before RNG use. The EAEC0 suffix tests EAX then assigns ECX and DX before using them.
caller_bridge.return_type: EC4A0 default returns the full EAX from EC990. Integer C interfaces retain partial-AL/AX and child return bit patterns.

limitations: Read-only Ghidra did not identify EAE20, 49E8B0 and 41CD00 procedures. Their existing raw byte/source models provide additional explicitly identified callsites; provider incoming references alone are incomplete there.

This exact native/source audit does not certify arbitrary caller-stack aliases, self-modifying code, corrupted private locals, unknown indirect callers, unused volatile outputs or OS exception dispatch.
